Loss of function in ALDH4A1 disrupts proline metabolism, leading to the accumulation of proline and its precursor, glutamate-gamma-semialdehyde. This disruption indirectly impacts one-carbon metabolism by altering substrate availability for tetrahydrofolate-dependent reactions. Concurrently, loss of function in GNMT leads to altered glycine metabolism, specifically affecting the methylation of glycine to sarcosine. This process is also linked to one-carbon metabolism, as GNMT activity influences the availability of methyl groups and tetrahydrofolate cofactors. The convergence occurs at the level of tetrahydrofolate metabolism, where dysregulation in both pathways can lead to imbalances in essential one-carbon units required for various biosynthetic processes, ultimately manifesting as distinct but mechanistically linked disease phenotypes.

partners.mechanism_chain: ALDH4A1 (HGNC:394) —DISRUPTS→ Proline (CHEBI:16860); Proline (CHEBI:16860) —LEADS_TO→ Glutamate metabolism (GO:0006537); Glutamate metabolism (GO:0006537) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperprolinemia type 2 (MONDO:0009401); AGXT2 (HGNC:288) —DISRUPTS→ beta-aminoisobutyric acid (CHEBI:15817); beta-aminoisobutyric acid (CHEBI:15817) —LEADS_TO→ Glutamate metabolism (GO:0006537); Glutamate metabolism (GO:0006537) —LEADS_TO→ beta-aminoisobutyric acid, urinary excretion of (MONDO:0008860).
